title: The Light
speaker: Josh Wyatt
card_summary: Josh opens Go Tell It in John 1:1-5. The risen Jesus opens Scripture on the Emmaus road, turning burning hearts into witnesses. The eternal Word is God, personally distinct, Creator, life, and unconquered light. Know him through his word, receive him, and go tell what you have seen and heard.
section_intro: The sermon begins at 00:09. Josh names the Advent assignment, builds the series from the Emmaus response, reads John 1:1-5, calls listeners to the Light, and closes in prayer at 42:09. The outline preserves that order and every confirmed Scripture use.

movements.heading: Advent purpose: know Jesus, then go tell it
bullets: Josh announces three weeks in the first half of John 1, ending with a Christmas Eve look at the nativity in Luke 2. The Advent challenge is simple: go tell it.
He trusts the Holy Spirit to create opportunities and wants to equip the church for them. To tell someone about Jesus, believers must know him; to go tell it, they must first have heard it.
The incarnation is either fantasy or creation’s decisive event. Christians are either pitiable fools or heralds of the most important news in human history.

movements.heading: God explains God through his written word
bullets: Josh says the series is not an apologetic. Scripture assumes the Creator, begins with God speaking light into darkness, and treats suppression of that reality as culpable rather than neutral.
Ancient philosophical schools disagreed about the divine but did not deny divine presence. A telephone-game illustration shows why human retelling drifts without the Holy Spirit and the written word.

Believers are born again and made new. Ephesians identifies the church’s foundation as the apostles and prophets with Christ as cornerstone—not feelings, wishes, or cultural approval. God explains God.

movements.heading: The Emmaus response: opened Scripture, burning hearts, immediate witness
bullets: Josh follows the disappointed travelers in Luke 24. Jesus restrains their recognition, rebukes their failure to believe Scripture, and explains from Moses and the Prophets what all Scripture says about him.

Moses, Joshua, Jericho, and Rahab become a gospel pattern: law can bring people to the promise, but Yeshua brings them in; judgment terrifies the rebellious city while the promised rescue gives Rahab joy.

When Jesus opens Scripture, eyes open and hearts burn. The travelers return immediately to testify. Jesus then supplies bodily evidence of resurrection, opens the Law, Prophets, and Psalms, and sends witnesses with promised power.

Repentance is not regret or payment. Christ finished the work; repentance is a Spirit-worked reorientation that releases sin to receive forgiveness. The church cannot tell what it has not seen and heard.

movements.heading: The life-giving Christ fulfills Scripture and awakens worship
bullets: The congregation reads John 1:1-5. John presents the divine Word as Creator, life, and unconquered light, selecting signs and scenes so readers recognize the Son of God.
Jesus fulfills Old Testament types: Lamb, ladder, temple, new birth, and the lifted serpent. At the cross God turns the curse into the cure—death becomes life for those made alive by grace.

Josh refuses to let familiarity shrink eternal life. Psalms, Revelation, and Zephaniah portray loud praise with voices and instruments as a response to deliverance, victory, God’s greatness, and salvation’s joy.

movements.heading: The eternal Word is God, personally distinct, and Creator
bullets: Only eternal God can give eternal life. John says the Word existed before creation, was with God, and was God. Jesus reveals the Father, is Alpha and Omega, and is God’s climactic speech to humanity.

Logos spoke to both Jewish and Greek hearers. Jesus’ claim to exist before Abraham confirms John’s testimony and exposes the doctrine of the Trinity: Father, Son, and Spirit are God yet personally distinct.
Josh warns against denying Christ’s deity or his personhood, rejects the Jehovah’s Witness rendering of John 1:1, and urges kind but firm gospel witness.
All things were made through the Word. God spoke creation into being through Christ, so Jesus is not created; only Jesus can offer eternal life.

movements.heading: The Light cannot lose: believe, receive, and come
bullets: Christ does not merely possess or give life; he is life. He enters the darkness of evil, unbelief, sin, and death, yet darkness cannot overcome him.
Everyone begins in darkness, but believers become children of light. Josh rejects fear-driven Christianity: the world has always been dark, the Lord still says not to fear, and the light cannot lose.

He asks whether listeners know, trust, and have received Jesus. The way was refused, the truth disbelieved, and the life crucified, yet those who receive him are given the right to become God’s children.
C. T. Studd’s line presses one lasting decision: only one life will soon pass, and only what is done for Christ will last. Believe in the light and come to Christ today.

movements.heading: Prayer for return, opened eyes, and Advent hope
bullets: Josh thanks the Father for Scripture and the incarnation: Christ takes flesh, lives the life sinners could not, dies the death they deserved, and gives a future promise.
He clings to Christ’s prepared place and return, asks that Christmas draw the church closer rather than pass as another holiday, and prays that those who have wandered will turn back.
Calling Jesus the light of the world, he asks God to open eyes, hearts, and minds so hearers believe, then entrusts the response to God’s will.

ledger.phrase: “the nativity of Jesus as described in Luke chapter 2”
If the incarnation is fiction, “everyone should pity us”; Christians are either fools or heralds of decisive news.
God’s reality is “obvious,” humanity has “no excuse,” and denial of the Creator is attributed to pride.
“In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth… ‘Let there be light,’ and there was light.”
“If you’ve been born again, if you’ve received new life through a second birth…”
“then you are a new creation”
“through him we both have access to the Father by one Spirit… built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the chief cornerstone”
Two believers leave Jerusalem for Emmaus after Jesus’ death and reports of the empty tomb.
“these two believers were kept from recognizing him”
Jesus asks what they are discussing; a traveler responds as though Jesus has been “living under a rock.”
“How foolish you are, and how slow to believe all that the prophets have spoken! Did not the Messiah have to suffer these things and then enter his glory?”
“beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he explained to them what was said in all the Scriptures concerning himself”
Moses brings Israel to the promised land but does not take them in; Joshua succeeds him and leads them forward.
Jericho fears Israel’s approach and trumpets, while Rahab trusts the promised deliverance and is saved.
“the new covenant purchased by the blood of Christ”
“Come, Lord Jesus. We are not afraid. We are expectant.”
Their eyes are opened, Jesus disappears, and they ask, “Were not our hearts burning within us… [as he] opened the Scriptures to us?”
“They got up and returned at once to Jerusalem… ‘It is true’… Then the two told what had happened on the way.”
“Peace be with you… Look at my hands and my feet… A ghost does not have flesh and bones”; Jesus eats fish.
“the same Jesus who fed 5,000 with a young boy’s lunch”
The Law, Prophets, and Psalms must be fulfilled; the Messiah suffers and rises; repentance and forgiveness are preached to all nations; witnesses await power from on high.
“It is finished. It is done.”
“What the world calls freedom, we now see as chains… only slaves of God are truly free.”
“Jesus just introduced the ministry of reconciliation.”
“Even the good man fails the Ten Commandments test.”
“In the beginning was the Word… In him was life… The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.”
If everything Jesus did were recorded, “the world wouldn’t have enough space for all the books.”
“Jesus is the Lamb of God”
Jesus is “the ladder from heaven to earth.”
“He is the new temple.”
“He gives new birth.”
“Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, that everyone who believes may have eternal life in him.”
The people are judged by serpents, and the image of the curse becomes God’s means of healing.
“the wages of sin is death”
“without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness”
“because of his great love for us, God, who is rich in mercy, made us alive with Christ… It is by grace you have been saved.”
“The death of the Son offers life to the world… everyone who believes may have eternal life in him.”
“Clap your hands, all peoples. Shout to God with loud songs of joy, for the Lord, the Most High, is to be feared, a great King over all the earth.”
“trumpets, lutes… harps, tambourines, strings, pipes, loud clashing cymbals”
“the roar of a great multitude in heaven shouting: ‘Hallelujah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God.’”
“The Lord your God is in your midst, a mighty one who will save… he will exult over you with loud singing.”
“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.”
“Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?”
“I am the Alpha and Omega,” explained as the first and last letters and as Christ’s self-description.
God has spoken by his Son, through whom he made the universe; the Son is the radiance of glory, exact representation, sustainer, purifier, and enthroned Lord.
“the Word was with God and the Word was God. He was with God in the beginning.”
“Before Abraham was born, I am”; they pick up stones to stone him.
“God the Spirit [was] also present before creation.”
Arianism is rejected because “the Word was God.”
Modalism is rejected because “the Word was with God”; Father and Son coexist in fellowship.
“Jesus is fully God and fully man… 100% God and 100% man.”
“They translate John 1:1 as ‘the Word was a god.’”
“I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is no one like me.”
“Through him all things were made; without him nothing was made that has been made.”
“God said, ‘Let there be,’ and there was.”
“For he spoke, and it came to be; he commanded, and it stood firm.”
“God created all things through Jesus Christ,” so Jesus is not created but eternal God.
“In him was life… The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness… has not overcome it.”
“I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
“God is light.”
“people love either the light or the darkness, and what they love informs how they behave”
Jesus, the light, enters evil, unbelief, sin, and death, yet darkness does not overcome him.
“I have come into the world as a light, so that no one who believes in me should stay in darkness.”
“While you have the light, believe in the light, that you may become sons of light.”
“Many have seen him. Many have heard him, but they’ve rejected him.”
“I am the way… I’m the truth… I’m the life,” followed by humanity’s refusal and crucifixion of him.
God gives believers “the right… to become children of God.”
“you must receive him… believe in his name”
“the incarnation… you taking on flesh to become the Christ”
“You know where I’m going… I’m going there to prepare a place for you,” with hope in Christ’s return.
“You are the light of the world.”
